clue.text: Seabirds and golfer harassed former WI captain

indicators.note: something harassed is pushed about and troubled, so the letters before it are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket legend from the Caribbean is pestered by gulls and a man playing golf.
explanation.walkthrough: WI is West Indies, the Caribbean cricket team; Sir Garfield (Garry) Sobers was its great all-rounder and captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobers led the West Indies Test cricket side in the 1960s and early 1970s, so he is a past skipper of that team.

clue.text: Prince with class next to Lamp-post singer

indicators.note: being next to something means sitting beside it, so the pieces are placed one after another

parts.note: George is the name of a British prince
a form is a school class
by can mean beside, next to

explanation.surface: A royal and his schoolmates stand beside a street light where someone is singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next to' does double duty: it gives BY and also places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Formby, a British ukulele-playing comedian, had a famous song called Leaning on a Lamp-post, so he is identified by that hit.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading the word from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: lager is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: Finish your beer at the pub called the King's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink up' reads as an instruction to finish a glass; here 'up' turns the drink round. The King's is a typical pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belonging to or befitting a monarch is described as royal or kingly, which is the adjective's meaning.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: out on the Spanish Main, the Caribbean sea route of old galleons
second meaning: on the whole, mostly

explanation.surface: A sailor who generally cruises off the Spanish coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'on the whole', and literally places a ship out on the Main, the old name for Caribbean waters.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: permission, liberty officially allowed
second meaning: abuse of freedom, lack of restraint

explanation.surface: A debate over whether some liberty is acceptable or goes too far.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means formal permission to act, and also unrestrained behaviour that oversteps proper limits, as in poetic or sexual excess.

clue.text: Tanner wastes Palm Sunday taking 24 hours off

indicators.note: to waste is to ruin or squander, so the remaining letters are wrecked into a new order
taking something off means removing it, so a portion of the phrase is stripped away

parts.note: taken as written
a day lasts 24 hours

explanation.surface: A leather tanner idles away the Sunday before Easter by taking the day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanner' looks like a leather worker; it is a device that gives you a tan. 'Taking ... off' wraps the words to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultraviolet lamp bronzes the skin, so it is a device that makes people brown, a tanner.

indicators.note: something running through another passes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: BR is an abbreviation for Britain
a ria is a drowned river valley

explanation.surface: A pipeline laid along a valley across the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco pipe carved from the root of the heath plant is called by that plant's name.

clue.text: Author making way round lake with boy turning up holding hands, at first

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: a road is a way
L is the abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
holding something means keeping it inside, so a piece is placed within another

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before

parts.note: first letter of hands

explanation.surface: A writer builds a road round a lake while a boy turns up holding hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers in a row: the first name is built by wrapping, then the surname by turning a word round and wrapping again.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory and many other children's books, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Should mean the end of most of the dry season

indicators.note: keeping only the end, the larger part, means the opening of the word is chopped away

parts.note: a drought is a long dry season

explanation.surface: A forecast claiming the dry spell ought to be nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first two letters DR of DROUGHT and the bulk that is left, its end, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are modal verbs of obligation: you should do it and you ought to do it say the same thing.

indicators.note: placed in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cut is an old name for a canal
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A man-eating creature with an author caught in a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like an injury; in British usage a cut is a man-made waterway, and the writing tool sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who eats human flesh is literally an eater of people, so the term fits exactly.

clue.text: It doesn't come as much of a blow

definitions.text: It doesn't come as much of a blow

parts.words: It doesn't come as much of a blow
parts.note: surface reading: some news that is not much of a shock or setback
setter's reading: a blow is a wind, and this is a mild one, a soft wind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' reads as a misfortune, but it means a wind that blows, here a mild one.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Beaufort scale this name describes force three, a light wind that hardly counts as a gale.

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a galley is a ship's kitchen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A half-built kitchen aboard an old ship of the Armada year.
explanation.walkthrough: 1588 is the year of the Spanish Armada.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish Armada of 1588 was a fleet largely of large sailing warships of this type.

clue.text: Cut short a game with partners from all quarters

parts.note: taken as written

parts.words: game with partners from all quarters
parts.note: bridge is a card game of two partnerships sitting North-South and East-West

explanation.surface: A card game with players drawn from every corner is brought to an early end.
explanation.walkthrough: The quarters are the compass points: bridge players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text or event by removing parts is to condense or truncate it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Oil hostilities cut short by mufti's decree

indicators.note: something cut short loses its tail, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: fat is an oil, a grease
war is a state of hostilities

explanation.surface: A conflict over oil ended early by a religious ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A mufti is an Islamic legal scholar, and a formal legal ruling he issues has this Arabic name.

parts.note: surface reading: the outstanding member of a group of people
setter's reading: a literal bunch of fruit, whose uppermost member is the boss

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'bunch' is also a cluster of the yellow fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means the most important person, the boss or leader, and literally names the highest fruit on the hand.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pawn capture made on the square passed over
second meaning: French for in passing, incidentally

explanation.surface: Someone casually mentions a chess move as an aside.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means 'in passing', used in English as an incidental remark and as the name of a special pawn capture.

clue.text: He may recommend Veuve Cliquot at river to one in ambush?

parts.note: the Somme is a river in northern France
one in ambush lies in wait, so is a lier

explanation.surface: A wine waiter suggesting champagne by the riverside to someone lying in wait.
explanation.walkthrough: Veuve Clicquot is a champagne house; the clue's spelling drops a C.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine waiter advises diners on what to drink, and a famous champagne would be among his suggestions; an example-style definition.

clue.text: Contrite traveller coming in, dropping a bit of rubbish

parts.note: a rep is a travelling salesman

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it fall away, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: an entrant is someone coming in

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of rubbish

explanation.surface: A sorry traveller arrives and lets fall some litter.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorrow and regret for a wrong you have done is being remorseful, the same sense as the clue word.

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: Audi is a make of car
a tor is a rocky hilltop

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper drives up to the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inspects a firm's financial records is a professional in the numbers trade, a kind of accountant.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the nickname of Frank Tyson, a very fast English bowler of the 1950s

explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like an adjective meaning candid; it is a first name, and the question mark admits the nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent tropical cyclone is a great whirling storm, and the same name was the nickname of fast bowler Frank Tyson.

indicators.note: half of a word means only one of its two halves survives, the other is discarded
after places one piece behind the other in reading order

parts.note: taken as written
lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: A fragment of a refuge found after the interval in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fragment; it means a fight. Keep the back half of TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused brawl or tussle among many people is a fight, which is the informal sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Broke right away, left high and dry

indicators.note: something sent away is gone, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: to breach is to break through
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone bankrupt quickly abandoned and stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' reads as penniless; it is the past tense of break.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat hauled or washed up onto the shore is stranded out of the water, which the idiom describes.

clue.text: Damp smell I detect at first

parts.note: a hum is a bad smell in British slang
taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before

parts.note: first letter of detect

explanation.surface: Someone notices the musty odour of a damp room.
explanation.definitionFit: Air full of moisture feels muggy and wet, so the adjective is a near synonym of the clue word.

definitions.note: adjective phrase: of the highest rank

indicators.note: something short is missing its tail, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a premiere is a first performance

explanation.surface: A brief first appearance for a player in a top division.
explanation.walkthrough: England's top football division is the Premier League.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means first in rank or importance, belonging to the leading division or class.

clue.text: Dramatist featured in Swinburne's biography, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the letters are read backwards
something featured in a passage appears within it, so the letters lie inside these words

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A playwright gets a mention in a life of the poet Swinburne.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian who wrote A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler, so he was a playwright.

indicators.note: cooked food is transformed and mixed, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something being cooked in a metal pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State tree' reads as a tree in a state of being; it is the official tree of a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: This fan-leaved palm is the official tree of South Carolina, which shows it on its flag.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: offspring, a legal term
second meaning: a matter in dispute

explanation.surface: The kids are the subject of a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are legally termed one's progeny, and a disputed point under debate is a matter or topic, both senses of the word.

indicators.note: made from means formed out of raw material, so the letters are reshaped into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Produce picked in an orchard in Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: This small loose-skinned citrus, like a tangerine, is a fruit grown originally in China.
